ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is an AC input of about 220V, 50Hz, coupled through a transformer to the secondary winding on the right side, and the secondary-side voltage is marked as u2; the upper end of the secondary winding is connected through a rectifier diode VD to the positive output terminal; at the output terminal there is a capacitor C connected in parallel with a load resistor RL, and the voltage across the load is marked as uL. Reasoning: This structure is a typical half-wave rectifier capacitor filter circuit. The given U2=20V in the problem is the RMS value of the transformer secondary voltage, and RLC satisfies the relatively large filtering condition RL C >= (3~5). According to the commonly used empirical relation of a half-wave rectifier capacitor filter circuit, the average value of the output DC voltage is approximately equal to the RMS value of the secondary voltage, namely ūL≈U2. Therefore ūL=20V.
